The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[-2,4],$ is shown above. It consists of three line segments. Find the average value of $f(x)$ on $[-2,4].$
question.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-2}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,1].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,4].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-3.
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2} \\  & =3-3 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4-(-2)}\cdot 0 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
